record.original_question: If X is a class of groups, let H(X) denote the class of homomorphic images of groups in X, let S(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in X, let P(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to(unrestricted) direct products of families of groups in X, and let Pf(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in X. By Birkhoff’s theorem, H(S(P(X))) is the variety of groups generated by X. If M is a class of metabelian groups, must H(S(Pf(M))) ⊆ S(H(P(S(M))))? This is Question 27 in(G. M. Bergman, Algebra Universalis, 26(1989), 267–283).

artifact.status_search_result: The question originates as Question 27 in G. M. Bergman's 1989 paper in Algebra Universalis (vol. 26, pp. 267–283), which established that HSP ≠ SHPS in general for metabelian groups while leaving several refined inclusions open. It is listed as a new problem in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook of unsolved problems in group theory, indicating that no resolution is known. No published solution was located.
